remarks.name: Boris Cherny
remarks.role: Claude Code anthropicai
remarks.text:
More details for the formal methods people -- what's happening is Claude is doing something like:

1. Building a model of the program, targeting a tricky state machine or race-prone part of the code
2. Finding counter-examples in the model. These are suspected bugs
3. Reproducing the bugs
4. Fixing the bugs in the code

It's not that the whole codebase is formally verified (yet!..), more that the hairiest parts of the code are modeled, checked for counter-examples, and fixed.
remarks.translation: 给形式化方法领域的人更多细节——正在发生的事情是Claude在做类似这样的事情：1. 构建程序的一个模型，针对代码中棘手的状态机或容易发生竞态的部分 2. 在模型中找到反例。这些是疑似bug 3. 复现这些bug 4. 在代码中修复这些bug。并不是说整个代码库都被形式化验证了（还！……），更多的是代码中最棘手的部分被建模、检查反例并修复。

remarks.name: Aditya Agarwal
remarks.role: General Partner SPC, Co-Founder Bevel_Health
remarks.text:
It tells you a lot when someone has moved around a lot in their career.

Also tells you a lot when there is low company turnover.

A team that has been working together for 3+ years is significantly higher throughput and more resilient than a team that has just formed.

A key mistake I see investors/employees make all the time is to simply ask about team size as opposed to team longevity.

AUC for teams is the right metric.
remarks.translation: 当某人在职业生涯中频繁跳槽，这能说明很多问题。同样，公司人员流动率低也能说明很多问题。一个已经合作了3年以上的团队，其产出效率显著更高，也更具韧性，远胜于一个刚刚组建的团队。我经常看到投资者/员工犯的一个关键错误是，只问团队规模，而不问团队的合作时长。团队的AUC才是正确的衡量指标。

podcasts.excerpt: 几年前，加州理工学院教授、Accelerated Understanding联合创始人Anima Anandkumar着手开发首个基于AI的开源天气模型。在与该领域专家交流时，她遇到了质疑。天气是混沌的，物理模拟很难，已经发展了几十年，而且需要超级计算机，数据根本不够。尽管有这些保留意见，Anima还是坚持前行并开始构建。不到一年，她的团队就开发出了FourCastNet，一个能与现有最佳物理模拟相媲美的预测模型。多亏了Anima及其后续工作，现在任何人都可以使用消费级GPU在短时间尺度上准确预测天气。在我们发布的约十五集科学节目中，<a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
